set.body:
Objective

Lift effectagram's universal numerical object from a packed symmetric self-geometry to a bilinear effect form between two named experimental spaces, while preserving geometry() as the public constructor and symmetric packed geometry as the optimized self-case.

Target architecture

relation families -> ordered measured relation pairs -> effect forms -> pair queries

A compiled task carries distinct left and right relation families, ordered partition edges, a measurement bridge, an edge operation, an explicit partition reducer, and an axis-bound query H. Gamma, H, the bridge, and the edge operation remain separate semantic objects and all enter the scientific plan identity.

Required outcomes

- One logical effect-form result with named left_space and right_space; self-form, symmetry, and guaranteed positivity are capabilities.
- Rectangular queries are universal; bilinear_query() remains the symmetric self-space compatibility constructor.
- Symmetric packed and rectangular storage are physical codecs, while complete form and query-only remain different result capabilities.
- The primitive kernel forms ordered outer products and never symmetrizes implicitly.
- Existing self-geometry behavior is recovered as a proven specialization.
- Compiler lowerings cover bilinear, centered bilinear, normalized bilinear, and required-edge materialization without an engine registry.
- Cross-neural-space evaluation requires an explicit factorized bridge into a common measurement space.
- Pair-space match/control and GLM constructors compile to H rather than creating ER-RSA classes.

Epic acceptance

- Self-specialization, transpose, direct-sum, packed-versus-rectangular, linear-fusion, query-invariance, explicit-centering, bridge, and no-bridge laws pass against independent numerical oracles.
- Tests demonstrate the noncommutation of correlation and Fisher transformation with partition reduction.
- Existing public self-geometry tests and installed-package workflow remain compatible within the declared numerical contract.
- Dense/sparse frames, feature blocking, memory/block storage, and direct/late query paths agree.
- Axis, bridge, reducer, edge-operation, and query failures occur before source reads.
- Scientific plan hashes and receipts identify both axes, ordered partition edges, bridge, edge pipeline, reducer, materialization, and query.
- Memory benchmarks cover every new sufficient-statistic plan and sparse query support.
- Public documentation explains geometry as the self-form specialization and demonstrates one unequal-axis bipartite workflow.

Deferred non-goals

No ER-RSA model or engine; no arbitrary dense cross-operator; no learned alignment or hyperalignment; no inference that treats pair edges as independent; no automatic balanced optimal-transport controls in the first delivery; no silent aggregate-first normalization; and no weakening of effect-space, neural-domain, source-revision, completeness, or receipt contracts.

Completion

The epic closes only after the independent certification child verifies semantic, numerical, resource, compatibility, documentation, and installed-artifact evidence.
set.title: Epic: Lift geometry to a universal bilinear effect form
